Harmattan Morning

The harmattan wind sweeps the red earth,
and dust settles soft on roof and leaf.
Old women wrap their cloths close at dawn,
while children cough and hurry on.

The sun climbs slow, a pale gold coin,
through haze that hides the hills from view.
Yet in the barns the yams lie safe,
and hope, like grain, is stored there too.

content:
The New Teacher

When Mr. Ade arrived at the village school, the pupils stared. He carried no cane, and his bag was full of books with bright covers. On his first day, he asked the class what they wanted to learn, and the room fell silent. No teacher had ever asked them that. Slowly, a small girl at the back raised her hand. 'I want to learn how to write a letter to my brother in Lagos,' she said. Mr. Ade smiled. 'Then we shall begin with letters,' he said. By the end of the term, every pupil had written a letter, and the small girl's brother had written back.
